scope: Second timing pass across ten motions and three characters
coverage: Four matched side phases and one portrait phase per motion across all three characters; native support audit at every authored frame; browser playback and source agreement. Phase views do not establish subjective 1x pacing or biomechanical realism.

bite.review: Jaw opening distinguishes the bite from lunge, followed by closure and recovery. Portrait is more informative than the small side view.

flee.review: The turn is visible before the running stance; portrait view exposes the limbs better after the subject turns away.

idle.review: Quiet alert stance remains readable across all three bodies; the small breath change is intentionally subtle.

look.review: Head direction changes against planted feet. Portrait view conveys the turn more clearly than the side silhouette.

lunge.review: The lowered preparation, forward chest drive and regained stance remain distinct; the revised camera includes Moss's muzzle.

roll.review: Lowering, flank/back contact and regaining the feet remain distinct on all three bodies; tucked limbs clear the visible silhouette.

run.review: Gathered and extended limbs distinguish the gallop from trot, with a visible airborne phase in the sampled poses.

swipe.review: The lifted forepaw distinguishes the strike from lunge and bite, with three supporting paws. This is a stylized combat gesture.

trot.review: Diagonal exchange stays legible on both long and short legs. The torso remains restrained rather than taking on the gallop gesture.

walk.review: Alternating planted and lifted paws remain distinct. The modest cadence increase preserves the walking gesture.
